A leafnode operator could cause trace events to be sent to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and could use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages.

title: Fabio: Access-control bypass through unnormalized request paths
description:
Summary

Route selection uses the raw un-normalized request path, and the per-route ACL and basic-auth gates hang off that selection, so a dot-segment, encoded-dot, or double-slash variant of a protected path selects a different route, skips both gates, and is forwarded to the backend which normalizes and serves the protected resource. title: appium allows unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion in @appium/storage-plugin
description:
Summary

The Appium storage plugin exposes an HTTP endpoint POST /storage/delete that takes a user-supplied name and deletes it from the server storage folder. The handler passes name straight into path.join(storageRoot, name) and then fs.rimraf() without any path sanitization. By sending a name containing ../ sequences, an unauthenticated remote client can escape the storage root and recursively delete arbitrary files and directories that the Appium process user can write, anywhere on the host filesystem.

The same plugin's *upload* path validates the name via fs.sanitizeName (requireValidItemOptions), but the *delete* path does not an asymmetry that makes the missing validation unambiguous.

title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
description:
Summary

svg2rlg() expands references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (CircularRefError). A group containing N elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10.

This is the SVG variant of the XML "billion laughs" attack (the same class as librsvg CVE-2019-20446).

title: go-guerrilla crashes on a bare XCLIENT command (7-byte slice off-by-one panic)
description:
The defect

Confirmed at HEAD. server.go: cmdXCLIENT = []byte("XCLIENT") is 7 bytes (line 78), so the dispatch match cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd) only guarantees len(input) >= 7. The handler then slices input[8:] (line 586):

 case sc.XClientOn && cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd):
 if toks := bytes.Split(input[8:], []byte{' '}); len(toks) > 0 { // line 586

A client sending the bare command XCLIENT (exactly 7 bytes) hits input[8:7] and panics runtime error: slice bounds out of range [8:7]. handleClient runs in the per-connection goroutine (server.go:391) which has no recover(); the only recover() calls are in the backend mail-processing workers (a different goroutine never reached during command parsing), so the unrecovered panic crashes the whole SMTP daemon.

title: Refitter: Unrestricted OpenAPI references permit build-host SSRF and file inclusion
description:
Summary

Refitter (the refitter dotnet tool, built on NJsonSchema for $ref resolution) fetches remote
http(s) URLs and reads local files (including absolute paths and ../ traversal outside the input
directory), inlining the referenced schema into the generated Refit interface/contracts. Running
refitter --output Out.cs on a spec whose $ref points at an attacker/internal URL or an
arbitrary local file yields SSRF, remote file inclusion, and local file inclusion. Verified on
Refitter 2.0.0.

Details

- $ref: http://attacker-or-internal/evil.json#/... -> build host fetches (SSRF) and inlines the
 remote schema (RFI); confirmed property REMOTE_REFIT_PROP.
- $ref: /abs/path.json#/... or ../../secret.json#/... -> out-of-tree local file read + inlined
 (LFI);

title: CKAN: Session Fixation in Registration View
description:
Description

Web user registration form is vulnerable to session fixation if the site is configured with server-side session storage (CKAN uses cookie-based session storage by default). The attacker would need to either set a cookie on the victim's browser or steal the victim's currently valid session. Session identifiers are now regenerated after registration.

Patches

This vulnerability has been fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6 and 2.12.0

Workarounds

switch to cookie-based session storage (the default) or disable web user registration by setting ckan.auth.create_user_via_web to false (the default)

description:
Summary

Extracting an attacker-supplied 7z archive can write files outside the destination directory. The 7z header stores each entry's path as a UTF-16 name with nothing constraining it to a relative, in-tree path. title: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
description:
Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

Patches
* 2.5.1

Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

Details
_Chain:_
1. POST /tlm/query writes the user-controlled fields value into fields_in.txt under the AIT-GUI static directory.
 * If the supplied dataDir has no .pcap files, the route returns the expected 400 Bad Request

title: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
description:
Summary

An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.

Daptin's generic entity list endpoint (GET /api/<entity>), which every table in a Daptin instance

validation as the fix for a previously published advisory

Impact ranges from unauthenticated denial of service (a single crafted request 500s the query) to
blind/error-based extraction of data from tables the requester has no permission to read.

            - 'httpd'

// SENTINEL APEX — CVE-2026-104199 Remote Code Execution Detection
// Product: Web Application | Generated: 2026-11-20T21:33:06Z
// Deploy to: Microsoft Sentinel / Defender XDR
let lookback = 1d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "tomcat.exe", "java.exe")
    and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "bash", "sh", "python.exe", "python3"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("wget http", "curl http", "certutil -urlcache", "bitsadmin /transfer"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update", "install", "backup", "deploy"))  // filter known-good
| extend Severity = "HIGH", CVE = "CVE-2026-104199", RuleSource = "SENTINEL-APEX"
| order by Timestamp desc

title: TastyIgniter allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Unrestricted file upload in Media Manager

Media manager accepts .htaccess file which can be used to perform RCE.

Details
The file upload functionality from media manager somehow accepts .htaccess file. This file could be used to allow any extension to run PHP command. By doing so, it is possible to perform RCE.

- Create a .htaccess file with the following code.

 SetHandler application/x-httpd-php

POST /admin/media_manager HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8888

sec-ch-ua: "Not-A.Brand";v="24", "Chromium";v="146"

title: ruflo MCP bridge allows unauthenticated remote code execution in default Docker Compose deployments
description:
The MCP bridge shipping in ruflo/docker-compose.yml exposed POST /mcp with no authentication. The docker-compose defaults bound the bridge and MongoDB to all interfaces. Combined, an unauthenticated network attacker could invoke tools/call → terminal_execute inside the bridge container, obtain a shell as node (uid 1000), read every provider API key from the container env, spawn attacker-controlled swarms on the victim's keys, and persist a poisoned pattern into the AgentDB learning store that steers future AI outputs for all users of the instance.

The tool blocklist that mentions terminal_execute was enforced only in the autopilot flow. POST /mcp and POST /mcp/:group bypassed it.

Fixed in ADR-166 Phase 1-3 (branch security/adr-166-mcp-bridge-rce, PR #2521):
- Bind loopback by default; fail-closed on public-bind opt-in without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN
- Bearer auth middleware (timingSafeEqual constant-time compare)
- Server-side executeTool gate for terminal_execute (MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true op

title: pREST _groupby function-expression SQL injection (incomplete fix of CVE-2025-58450)
description:
What the fix did and the gap

The v2.3.0 fix (commit e88dabb) routed the _select field through a strict new gate, sanitizeSelectField (postgres.go:947/1003/2097). The sibling _groupby path was left on the far weaker isSafeSQLExpression. adapters/postgres/postgres.go, GroupByClause (line 1946): a _groupby field that contains balanced parens takes the raw-SQL-expression branch (around lines 1999-2006), gated only by isSafeSQLExpression (line 2001, defined at 2043). That gate validates only the OUTERMOST function name against a 13-entry allowlist and uses a character allowlist that permits spaces, single quotes and parens. It blocks ;, --, /* , unbalanced parens and an outer pg_ prefix, but NOT a trailing UNION SELECT ..., a nested (SELECT ...) subquery, or an inne

title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
description:
Impact

verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was
verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted
wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before /
not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate.
There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning.

A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was
signed by *whoever supplied the embedded certificate* — never that it was signed
by a *trusted* party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a
forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification.
Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be
impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass).

verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was not
affected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor came
from the message.

title: laradocs  Command injection via unescaped Node.js binary path in KaTeX SSR
description:
Summary
Local command injection (CWE-78) in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a proc_open() command string.

Affected versions
>= 0.4.0, < 1.0.0

Patched versions
>= 1.0.0 (fixed in commit 100cb1e)

Impact
When rendering KaTeX math server-side, Laradocs invoked Node via proc_open() with a command string in which the Node binary argument was not passed through escapeshellarg().

MarkdownPipelineFactory constructs KatexExtension with the configured binary, which the render path resolved as:

$node = $this->nodeBin ?? 'node';
$cmd = $node . ' ' . escapeshellarg($tmpFile) . ' ' . escapeshellarg($input);

$this->nodeBin comes from Config::nullableString('laradocs.parser.katex.node_bin'). Both possible sources — the configured node_bin value, or the 'node' default resolved from PATH — are operator-controlled. Neither is derived from untrusted request data or documentation content.

The vulnerable branch is reached only when server-side rendering is enabled.

title: GitHub CLI gh codespace jupyter may allow code execution via unvalidated URLs from malicious Codespaces
description:
Summary

A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow remote code execution when users connect to a malicious Codespace using the gh codespace jupyter command. The command opens JupyterLab by launching a URL in the user's browser, but that URL is supplied by a process running inside the Codespace and the CLI opens it without validating it.

title: etcd: CRL enforcement bypass on gRPC listener when --listen-client-http-urls is configured
description:
Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

When etcd is configured with --listen-client-http-urls to split the HTTP and gRPC client endpoints onto separate listeners, the --client-crl-file Certificate Revocation List is not enforced on the gRPC listener. A client presenting a revoked certificate is correctly rejected by the HTTP endpoint but continues to authenticate successfully over gRPC.

Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

This vulnerability is patched in the following versions:

- etcd 3.6.13
- etcd 3.5.32

Workarounds
_Is there a way for users to fix or remediate the vulnerability without upgrading?_

If upgrading is not immediately possible, reduce exposure by restricting network access to etcd client ports using firewall rules or network policy so that only trusted components can reach the server. This limits the pool of clients that could exploit a revoked certificate but does not enforce CRL revocation.

description:
Summary
When applying a delta object from a packfile, isomorphic-git reads a server-controlled targetSize and calls Buffer.alloc(targetSize) with no upper bound. title: secp256k1-native has a compiler-induced timing side channel in scalar multiplication
description:
Summary

Point#mul — the default, constant-time scalar multiplication and the library's headline secret-scalar operation — could leak timing information about the secret scalar (a private key or ECDSA-style nonce in a downstream consumer) not because of a source-level bug, but because the compiler reconstructed a branch from branchless source.

The Montgomery ladder selects between point candidates with uint256_select, written deliberately branchlessly as r = (a & ~mask) | (b & mask) with a mask that is all-ones or all-zeros. GCC 15.2 at -O2 recognises this select idiom, reconstructs the original boolean condition, and emits a secret-dependent conditional jump (je/jne). The branch's taken/not-taken timing correlates with the secret scalar bits flowing through the ladder.

This silently undid the 0.17.0 fix for the historical |t|=875 infinity-branch leak, which had relied on uint256_select compiling to branchless code.

title: i18next deepExtend recurses into inherited built-ins, allowing corruption of shared built-in objects (DoS)
description:
Summary

deepExtend in src/utils.js (reached via the public addResourceBundle(lng, ns, data, deep, overwrite) API) checked key existence with the in operator, which walks the prototype chain. A source key matching an inherited built-in (e.g. hasOwnProperty, toString, valueOf) therefore caused the function to recurse into the shared object on Object.prototype. With overwrite: true, a nested value could overwrite a property of that shared built-in — for example setting Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call to a non-callable value — corrupting it process-wide and causing an unrecoverable denial of service.

This is distinct from CVE-2026-48713 (i18next-fs-backend) and CVE-2026-48714 (i18next-http-middleware), which are prototype pollution via setPath/key-walking in different packages. title: Gradle causes failure to disable repositories exposing builds to malicious artifacts
description:
Impact

When resolving dependencies, Gradle searches repositories in declaration order. If it encounters connection errors, Gradle will disable the repository and fail dependency resolution. This is necessary for both reproducibility and security reasons to prevent dependencies from being resolved from other repositories without warning.

In previous versions of Gradle, some exceptions were not treated as fatal errors and would not cause a repository to be disabled. If a build encountered one of these exceptions, Gradle would continue to the next repository in the list and potentially resolve dependencies from a different repository.

title: Klever Go counts bitmap padding bits toward BLS quorum, allowing blocks with insufficient signatures
description:
Summary

When validating an incoming block header, HeaderSigVerifier.verifyConsensusSize counts *every* set bit in PubKeysBitmap — including bits that correspond to no validator (the padding bits of the final byte, which exist whenever the consensus group size is not a multiple of 8). The subsequent BLS aggregate-signature verification (blsMultiSigner.Verify) only checks signature validity for real validator indices and silently ignores those padding bits. As a result, a malicious or compromised block producer can set the padding bits to make the on-bits reach the PBFT quorum while only gathering a smaller number of real validator signature shares, causing a block to be accepted as correctly signed without a genuine two-thirds validator quorum.
